Design effect for clustered and crossover trials

Source: R/design_effect.R
compute_design_effect.Rd

Computes each study's design effect from its trial design. Effect sizes divide counts and sample sizes by it to give effective sample sizes; the reported sizes are kept unchanged in the data.

Usage

compute_design_effect(
  trial_design,
  ...,
  n_clusters = NA_real_,
  n_periods = NA_real_,
  n_total = NA_real_,
  cluster_size = NA_real_,
  rho_w = NA_real_,
  rho_b = NA_real_,
  rho_wp = NA_real_,
  labels = NULL
)

Arguments

trial_design

Trial design of each study.

...

Unused; must be empty.

n_clusters

Number of clusters, \(k\) above.

n_periods

Number of periods, \(p\) above.

n_total

Total sample size, n_int + n_ctrl, used with n_clusters.

cluster_size

Mean participants per cluster (per cluster-period for cluster crossover trials), m above. Overrides the value derived from n_clusters.

rho_w

Within-period intracluster correlation.

rho_b

Between-period intracluster correlation.

rho_wp

Within-person correlation across periods.

labels

Study labels used in messages.

Value

A numeric vector the same length as trial_design.

Details

trial_designDesign effect
"rct"\(1\)
"c_rct"\(1 + (m - 1)\rho_w\)
"xo_rct"\((1 - \rho_{wp}) / 2\)
"cxo_rct"\(1 + (m - 1)\rho_w - m\rho_b\)

where \(m\) is the mean cluster size (per cluster-period for cluster crossover trials). It is taken from cluster_size when given, and otherwise derived as \(m = n_{total} / (k \times p)\), where \(k\) is n_clusters and \(p\) is n_periods (1 for cluster trials and 2 for cluster crossover trials when n_periods is missing).

Missing inputs give a design effect of 1: a cluster crossover trial without rho_b uses \(\rho_b = 0\), and any design whose formula still cannot be evaluated (e.g. no rho_w or no cluster_size) is treated as 1. bayesma's names ("parallel", "cluster", "crossover", "cluster_crossover") are also accepted, and a missing design is treated as "rct".

For crossover trials the formula assumes that n_ctrl + n_int is the number of participants, so a trial of 40 participants is entered as 20 and 20.

Examples

compute_design_effect(c("rct", "c_rct", "xo_rct", "cxo_rct"),
                      n_clusters = c(NA, 10, NA, 10),
                      n_total = c(100, 200, 40, 400),
                      rho_w = c(NA, 0.05, NA, 0.05),
                      rho_wp = c(NA, NA, 0.6, NA))
#> [1] 1.00 1.95 0.20 1.95
